scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8841: Users report that "web0.local" and "web1.local" will not
load at all from host_1_1_1_1 -- the portals never come up. The team has decided
that all the web servers in the server farm must have crashed and wants every
web server rebooted. Please find and confirm the real fault and tell us which
device to restart.

injection.action: stop the BIND (named) DNS service on dns_server

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on dns_server: its BIND (named) service is stopped, so the
campus DNS no longer resolves names -- web0.local, web1.local and the other
*.local names fail to resolve, which is why the portals never load by name. The
ticket MISDIRECTS to the web servers, but the web servers are healthy: web_server_0
(10.200.0.3) and the other web servers are UP, reachable at the IP layer (ping
succeeds), and Apache is still serving HTTP on port 80. The symptom is purely
dead name resolution, not a web-server crash and not the network.

The correct diagnosis identifies dns_server (DNS/named service down) as the
faulty device and explicitly EXONERATES the web servers: they answer HTTP when
reached by IP, so the user's "all the web servers crashed" hypothesis is wrong.
An agent that reboots / blames web_server_0 (or the other web servers) has
followed the ticket's misdirection instead of the evidence.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the BIND DNS service on dns_server (e.g. `systemctl start named`). Once
named is resolving again, web0.local / web1.local resolve to their server IPs and
the portals load normally. The web servers need no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-dns-down: identifies the DNS/named service on dns_server is stopped (names do not resolve), not a web-server fault
bonus-exonerates-web-servers: notes the web servers serve HTTP when reached by IP, rejecting the "web servers crashed" hypothesis

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: The DNS service on dns_server (10.200.0.2) is down/not listening on port 53, so clients cannot resolve internal names.

Mechanism: Hosts rely on 10.200.0.2 for name resolution (host_1_1_1_1 resolv.conf points to 10.200.0.2). With DNS offline, lookups for web0.local and web1.local fail, so browsers “wait” on DNS and the portals never load by name. Connectivity to the servers themselves and HTTP service are fine, which is why direct access by IP works.

Localization: On host_1_1_1_1, getent/nslookup return no answers and show “connection refused” to 10.200.0.2:53. On dns_server, there is no process listening on UDP/TCP 53 (netstat/ss show nothing on :53), and no dnsmasq/bind/unbound process is running (ps check). Meanwhile, the web servers are healthy: both web_server_0 and web_server_1 have TCP 80 listening, and host_1_1_1_1 can ping and curl them by IP.

Root cause: The DNS daemon on dns_server has stopped/crashed (no listener on :53), leaving clients unable to resolve web0.local and web1.local.

Corrective fix: Restart the DNS service on dns_server (e.g., start/restart dnsmasq, or reboot the dns_server container/VM if needed), and ensure it is enabled to start at boot. After restart, verify that 10.200.0.2 is listening on :53 and that getent hosts web0.local/web1.local return 10.200.0.3/10.200.0.4 from clients. Also confirm the DNS configuration contains the required mappings for the web servers so name resolution remains functional. No web servers need rebooting.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies the DNS daemon on dns_server as stopped/not listening on port 53, shows evidence it's causing resolution failures, and exonerates the web servers.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-web-servers: notes the web servers serve HTTP when reached by IP, rejecting the "web servers crashed" hypothesis
per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly states the web servers are healthy and reachable by IP (TCP 80 listening, can ping/curl), rejecting the 'web servers crashed' hypothesis.
Proposes restarting the DNS service on dns_server and verifying resolution/listening, which matches the expected fix to bring named/dns service back up and restore name resolution.

Investigation log shows clients point at 10.200.0.2 for DNS, name lookups fail with “connection refused” to 10.200.0.2:53, and ss/netstat on dns_server show no listener on :53 while web servers respond to ICMP and have TCP:80 listening. The agent’s conclusion (DNS daemon on dns_server stopped; web servers healthy) follows directly from these observations.
